title: Trans-Blot Turbo Transfer with Home-made Buffers
author: Luisa F. Jiménez-Soto
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ghhbt36
materials: Anode buffer I 0,3 M Tris pH 10,4; 10% MethanolAnode buffer II 25 mM Tris pH 10,4; 10% MethanolCathode Buffer 25 mM Tris, 40 mM 6-Amino-n-Caproic acid, 10% Methanol, final pH 9,4 Methanol is toxic. Please protect you from direct contact or inhalation. http://www.cdc.gov/niosh/ipcsneng/neng0057.html
We use mini-protean gels (Bio-Rad). Our PVDF (0,22µm) membranes are 8,7 mm x 6,2 mm. The paper should have similar dimensions. Paper used: Kimberly Clark , WYPALL X60 (KC 6034)

We use the following times and conditions for the Turbo Blot transfer machine from Bio-Rad. 20 minutes at 1.3 A, Max. 25V for one mini-gel transfer 20 minutes at 2.5 A - Max. 25V for two minigels transfer. If your paper, buffers and membranes are working fine, you should have a constant 1,3 A (+/- 0,1) (one gel) of 2,5 A (+/- 0,2) (two gels) for the duration of the transfer.

steps.title: Activate Gel
steps.instruction: Activate the gel if using the Stain-Free system.

steps.title: Activate PVDF Membrane
steps.instruction: Prepare the membrane for transfer using methanol and anode buffer.

substeps.instruction: Activate the membrane in methanol for 15-30 seconds.
Transfer the membrane to Anode II buffer.
Ensure the membrane is fully immersed and does not float on the surface of the buffer.

steps.title: Prepare Transfer Stack
steps.instruction: Assemble the paper stack and remove air bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Arrange the paper in the stack according to the provided reference image.
Verify paper thickness (approximately 1 mm for two single layers).
Use a roller to remove all bubbles from between the stacks before running.

steps.title: Recover and Dry Membrane
steps.instruction: Remove the membrane from the cassette and dry to bind proteins.

substeps.instruction: Carefully remove the membrane from the cassette stack.
Dry the membrane for 1 hour at 37°C to bind proteins.
Avoid rubbing the surface of the membrane.

steps.title: Store Membrane
steps.instruction: Store the protein-bound membrane based on required duration.

substeps.instruction: Store at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
Store at -70°C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Reactivate Membrane for Western Blot
steps.instruction: Prepare the dried membrane for blocking while preventing dehydration.

substeps.instruction: Immediately follow with the blocking solution.
Perform methanol activation in the same container as blocking to prevent the membrane from drying and forming patches.
